messages:
maria: Heads up — starting ~11:09 we saw a tail latency jump on canary (short prompts p95 went from ~100ms to ~1.2s). Noticing this across several small-model routes :eyes:

deploy-bot: deployed kernel-selector v3 to canary cluster 'canary-eu-1' at 2025-08-01T11:07:40Z

devon: looking. any obvious infra noise? node cpu/mem stable?

sam: infra looks fine, but kvcache evictions spiked around the same time. metric: kvcache_evictions/sec  -> baseline ~5, spike ~42 from 11:08 onwards.

maria: here's the perf-bot alert and p95 timeline: https://metrics.internal/redwood/canary/tail-latency (shortlink)

perf-bot: alert: continuous-batcher tail-latency > 800ms on canary-eu-1 (triggered 11:10 UTC)

leo: kernel-selector v3 changed startup-cost weighting and now prefers fused kernels for short sequences in some configurations. Could be a startup overhead tradeoff.

anika: that matches my quick read — fused kernels reduce per-token work but have higher init overhead. For very small microbatches, selector might be choosing the wrong kernel.

devon: can anyone dump a profiler snapshot from canary? command I run:
```
./tools/profiler --cluster canary-eu-1 --service continuous-batcher --duration 30s --json > /tmp/canary-prof.json
```
I pulled a short profile, attaching snippet:
```
{"time":"11:09:45","op":"kernel_init","kernel":"fused-attn-v2","latency_ms":48}
{"time":"11:09:45","op":"kernel_init","kernel":"fused-attn-v2","latency_ms":52}
{"time":"11:09:46","op":"dispatch","microbatch_size":1,"dispatch_ms":12}
{"time":"11:09:47","op":"kvcache_evict","size":128}
```
That init cost is non-trivial for small MB sizes.

sam: also seeing microbatch distribution shift — fraction of microbatches of size 1 jumped from 18% to 46% after deploy. histogram: small-batches.png (posted).

maria: so two things: selector is picking fused kernels (higher init), and more tiny microbatches are happening -> higher dispatch/startup amortization -> tails. Why did tiny microbatches increase?

leo: I see the admission change in v3 — it relaxed pack-window heuristics to favor latency for some tenants, which inadvertently reduced packing for high-churn routes. Combined with scheduler preemption, that fragmenting increased number of size-1 batches.

anika: kvcache eviction pattern makes sense then: more ephemeral queries cause more unique KV keys, plus eviction churn due to smaller effective cache hits. That amplifies latency since cache misses hit model attention pathways.

devon: OK let's roll canary back to v2 while we triage. Plan: revert selector v3 image for canary-eu-1, monitor tail metrics for 10m, then capture baseline profile.

devon: running rollback:
```
kubectl -n runtime set image deploy/kernel-selector kernel-selector=redwood/kernel-selector:v2 --context=canary-eu-1
```

deploy-bot: rollback initiated. kernel-selector reverted to v2 on canary-eu-1 at 2025-08-01T11:18:04Z

maria: tail p95 trending back down — 11:22 snapshot p95 ~110ms. Looks like rollback helped.

perf-bot: recovery: continuous-batcher tail-latency back to baseline on canary-eu-1

devon: good. Root cause summary so far: v3's selector cost model underestimated kernel init overhead for fused-attn-v2 relative to dispatch frequency, combined with a packing heuristic change that increased microbatch fragmentation. Net effect -> higher startup costs, more kvcache churn, tail spikes.

leo: suggested fixes: 1) update kernel cost model to add explicit startup penalty term and measure amortization vs microbatch size, 2) add a minimum microbatch size floor or stronger pack-window for routes with high churn, 3) add automated canary checks: simulate small-microbatch workload and ensure p95 doesn't regress when switching selector.

anika: I'll own the cost-model tweak (small PR to add startup_penalty factor + unit tests against microbatch simulator). sam can you own a quick kvcache metric alert to detect eviction amplification?

sam: on it, I'll add an alert and a dashboard tile for eviction:hit_rate and eviction/sec correlated with pack size distribution.

maria: create a short postmortem doc and tag eng-runtime + eng-ml. We should also add a loadtest in CI that includes a high small-microbatch ratio to catch this class of regressions.

devon: thanks all. follow-ups: anika PR + perf sim, sam alert + dash, leo patch to pack-window default, I'll schedule a canary re-deploy only after the sim passes.

leo: quick note: maybe add a perf test that exercises fused-attn init cost specifically (cold-start microbatch path).

maria: agile next steps recorded in the incident board. Closing thread for now, reopen if rollback doesn't hold or if we see regressions in next deploy. :thumbsup:
